## How it works

- [statement] Pathogenic SNCA variants cause rare autosomal dominant PD; point mutations and gene multiplications are relevant variant classes. SNCA penetrance and phenotype depend on the variant. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10946878/ · keywords: Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1 · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Pathogenic LRRK2 variants cause autosomal dominant PD with reduced, age-dependent penetrance; inheriting a pathogenic variant does not guarantee disease. (medium confidence) — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/ · keywords: Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1 · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4501942/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10946878/
- [statement] Marder and colleagues (2015) estimated PD risk to age 80 at 0.26 (95% CI 0.18–0.36) in relatives predicted to carry LRRK2 G2019S in an Ashkenazi Jewish kin-cohort. This is an ancestry- and ascertainment-specific estimate, not universal penetrance for every LRRK2 variant. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4501942/ · keywords: Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1
- [statement] PRKN- and PINK1-related PD have autosomal recessive inheritance and are especially relevant in early-onset disease; established recessive disease must be distinguished from finding a single heterozygous variant. (medium confidence) — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/ · keywords: Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1 · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10946878/
- [statement] GeneReviews describes PRKN-related PD as usually beginning before age 35 with slow progression and relatively milder non-motor manifestations; PINK1-related PD has a similar phenotype, with psychiatric features more prominent. (low confidence) — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/ · keywords: Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1
- [statement] Large studies have not demonstrated increased PD risk from a single heterozygous pathogenic PRKN variant. The UK Biobank/NIH-PD study found similar PD likelihood in single-variant carriers and noncarriers; this does not establish recessive PRKN disease in a monoallelic carrier. (medium confidence) — https://www.ukbiobank.ac.uk/publications/heterozygous-prkn-mutations-are-common-but-do-not-increase-the-risk-of-parkinsons-disease/ · keywords: Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1 · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/
- [statement] In the 2024 PD GENEration publication, 8301 participants had received results from enrollment through June 2023; 13% had reportable variants and 9.1% of those without the specified high-risk factors had reportable variants. Reportable included pathogenic, likely pathogenic and risk variants, so the yield is not a count of confirmed monogenic diagnoses. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39074992/ · keywords: Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1
- [statement] GBA1 encodes the lysosomal enzyme glucocerebrosidase. Biallelic disease-causing variants are associated with Gaucher disease, whereas heterozygous variants can increase PD risk; these are different genetic counseling contexts. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12162886/ · keywords: Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1
- [statement] GeneReviews explicitly describes disagreement about classifying GBA1-associated PD as monogenic disease or a risk-factor association, while noting that some Gaucher-causing variants have higher penetrance. The classification should be qualified by variant and population. (low confidence) — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/ · keywords: Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1
- [statement] Heterozygous GBA1 variants increase PD risk with variable penetrance, whereas biallelic Gaucher-disease-causing GBA1 variants are associated with Gaucher disease. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12162886/ · keywords: Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1 · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/
- [statement] GBA1-associated PD risk depends on variant severity and genetic background; the UK Biobank/LuxPark study found that polygenic risk modified risk among carriers, so a single penetrance estimate should not be applied to every carrier. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12162886/ · keywords: Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1 · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/
- [statement] A meta-analysis of 17 datasets from Parkinson's disease genome-wide association studies in European ancestry samples identified 90 independent genome-wide significant risk signals across 78 genomic regions; these 90 variants explained 16-36% of the heritable risk of Parkinson's disease depending on prevalence. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31701892/ · keywords: Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] In the 2025 UK Biobank/LuxPark study, severe and mild GBA1 variant groups had nearly double the PD risk of the risk-variant group, and polygenic background further stratified risk. These are cohort associations rather than a deterministic individual prediction. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12162886/ · keywords: Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Heterozygous GBA1 variants increase PD susceptibility with variable penetrance influenced by age, variant and genetic background; a carrier result alone does not establish that PD will develop. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12162886/ · keywords: Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1 · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/
- [statement] PD panels need attention to copy-number analysis: sequencing alone may miss deletions or duplications, particularly relevant to SNCA and PRKN. Check whether the assay includes deletion/duplication testing. (medium confidence) — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/ · keywords: Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1 · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10946878/
- [statement] GBA1 coverage differs among laboratories: verify inclusion and full sequencing. Expanded testing can identify variants of uncertain significance that require expert interpretation and may remain inconclusive. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10946878/ · keywords: Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1
- [statement] Genetic counseling should explain inheritance, penetrance and test limitations. Expert review supports pretest and posttest counseling; GeneReviews specifically recommends discussing limitations and consequences before predictive testing of asymptomatic relatives. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10946878/ · keywords: Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1 · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/
- [statement] Testing beyond selected known variants can reveal variants of uncertain significance requiring expert interpretation; such findings may not establish pathogenicity. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10946878/ · keywords: Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1

## Research summary — Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1

PD genetics spans dominant LRRK2 and SNCA disease, recessive PRKN and PINK1 disease, and variably penetrant GBA1-associated susceptibility. Variant identity, age, ancestry and ascertainment affect interpretation. Genetic testing can identify trial-relevant subgroups, but reportable variants are not synonymous with confirmed monogenic diagnoses. Reliable interpretation requires appropriate copy-number and GBA1 coverage, distinction between monoallelic and biallelic findings, and genetic counseling. Cohort-specific penetrance estimates should not be treated as deterministic predictions for an individual. Genome-wide association studies add common-variant risk loci beyond the monogenic genes.

## Source disagreement — Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1

GeneReviews reports disagreement over classifying GBA1-associated PD as monogenic disease versus a risk-factor association because penetrance is low, particularly in population cohorts. GeneReviews notes that some Gaucher-causing GBA1 variants have PD penetrance approaching LRRK2 pathogenic variants.
